hints: Look at the two different functional groups in the fragment, the ester and the three C=C double bonds, and think which reagent attacks which.
Warm aqueous sulfuric acid hydrolyses the methyl ester $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ to a carboxylic acid $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ plus methanol, while the alkenes are unchanged.
Hydrogen with nickel catalyst then saturates every C=C to C-C but leaves the carboxylic acid alone, so count single bonds and check the acid group to pick the structure.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reactive groups in strobilurin**

The part shown has one methyl ester group, $\text{-CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, and three alkene C=C bonds. R and R' are inert, so they do nothing.

Starting fragment:
$$\text{R-CH=CH-CH=C(CH}_3\text{)-C(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)=CH-R'}$$

**Warm with aqueous acid to make X**

Warm aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is classic acid hydrolysis of an ester. The $\text{-OCH}_3$ is replaced by $\text{-OH}$.

$$\text{R'-CO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R'-CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
So compound X still has the three C=C bonds, but now has $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ instead of $\text{-CO}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Hydrogenate with H2 / Ni to make Y**

$\text{H}_2$ with Ni catalyst adds $\text{H}_2$ across each C=C, turning alkenes into alkanes. It does not reduce carboxylic acids under these conditions.

$$\text{C=C} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH-CH}$$
All three double bonds become single bonds, giving a fully saturated carbon skeleton:
$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CO}_2\text{H)-CH}_2\text{-R'}$$

**Match to the options**

That structure has a $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group, no $\text{OCH}_3$, no $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, and all single bonds in the chain. This matches only one option.

options.A: Correct. It shows the hydrolysed acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ and all three former C=C bonds fully hydrogenated to $\text{CH}_2\text{-CH}_2$ units, with R, R' and the methyl branch unchanged.
options.B: Wrong. It still contains $\text{OCH}_3$ and shows $\text{HO-CH(OCH}_3\text{)-}$ instead of a carboxylic acid. Acid hydrolysis removes methanol, it does not give a hemiacetal type group, and H2/Ni does not reduce a C=O in that way.
options.C: Wrong. It shows $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ (a primary alcohol) instead of $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. That would need a strong reducing agent like $\text{LiAlH}_4$ to reduce the ester or acid, but H2 with Ni does not reduce carboxylic acids or esters.
options.D: Wrong. It shows extra $\text{-OH}$ groups on the chain, as if water added across the C=C bonds. H2/Ni causes hydrogenation (adds H to each carbon), not hydration or hydroxylation, so no new C-OH bonds form on the alkene carbons.
